technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Shell as the command-line framework and implement only stream-oriented commands within the scope of this increment.
Use the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow REST API through a dedicated client/service layer rather than embedding server-side logic in the shell.
Represent module metadata using Spring Boot @ConfigurationProperties-compatible metadata and expose a generic strategy that can discover and render module properties for the module info command.
Port the Spring XD modules as Spring Cloud Stream-compatible source or processor modules while preserving their externally visible configuration semantics where practical.
Use the repository's existing build system, dependency-management conventions, test framework, coding standards, and supported Java version.
Provide unit tests for module behavior and shell/metadata logic, with focused integration tests for REST interaction and stream-module wiring.
assumptions: An existing Spring Cloud Data Flow or equivalent repository and build skeleton is available; this estimate does not include creating a new multi-module project from scratch.
The REST API contract and authentication requirements are sufficiently stable and documented for implementation without server-side REST changes.
Existing Spring XD source code and licensing-compatible implementation details are available for the http, tcp, twitterstream, twittersearch, filter, and transform modules.
The port will target the Spring Framework 6 and Java 17 baseline described in the specification, with necessary API and dependency migrations included.
Twitter modules may require credentials and external-service configuration, but production Twitter infrastructure, account setup, and live-service certification are excluded.
The stream shell scope includes core stream lifecycle and inspection operations such as create, deploy, undeploy, destroy, list, and display; advanced shell customization is excluded.
One developer performs analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and defect correction sequentially; estimates are effort in workdays, not elapsed time.
No major redesign of existing Spring Cloud Stream runtime behavior, server persistence, security, or deployment infrastructure is required.
Documentation is limited to command usage, module properties, configuration, migration notes, and examples sufficient for acceptance.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing project structure, build configuration, Spring Cloud Data Flow REST contracts, Spring Shell conventions, module packaging, and available Spring XD implementations; define implementation boundaries and compatibility mappings.
Implement the Spring Shell command layer and REST client/service integration for core stream commands, including argument parsing, validation, command output, error handling, and unit tests.

activities.activity_name: Module metadata strategy and module info command
activities.activity_description: Design and implement metadata discovery based on @ConfigurationProperties, map module descriptors and properties into a stable representation, implement the module info shell command, and add tests for property rendering and missing metadata.
Adapt the Spring XD http module to the target Spring Cloud Stream module conventions, migrate dependencies and configuration, implement source behavior, and add unit and focused integration tests.
Adapt the Spring XD tcp module, including TCP connection/listener behavior, configuration properties, lifecycle handling, dependency migration, and automated tests.
Migrate the Twitter streaming source, map credentials and filtering configuration, adapt its event-to-message behavior to the target stream model, and add tests using mocked Twitter interactions.
Migrate the Twitter search source, implement configuration and polling/search behavior compatible with the target framework, handle errors and message conversion, and add mocked-service tests.
Adapt the filter processor, preserve expression/configuration semantics where supported, integrate it with the target message pipeline, and add unit and stream-processing tests.
Adapt the transform processor, migrate configuration and transformation behavior, integrate it with the target message pipeline, and add unit and stream-processing tests.

Build end-to-end verification for shell-to-REST stream operations, module metadata discovery, module packaging, representative source-to-processor pipelines, configuration binding, and Java/framework compatibility; resolve integration issues found during testing.

Document shell commands, module metadata and properties, module migration/configuration details, credentials and operational constraints, and update build artifacts, descriptors, examples, and repository documentation.

activities.activity_name: Final quality assurance and defect correction
activities.activity_description: Perform clean-build verification, static checks, regression testing, acceptance review against all user stories, and correct remaining implementation, test, or documentation defects.
